[Post-Match Thread] LiverpoolFC vs AFC Bournemouth at Anfield

I honestly though we were far from convincing and were constantly at risk of getting run over, I can't imagine we will be taking 3 if we play like this in the next several games.

Clyne was wonderful, he had a nice attacking threat and was good defensively.

Good to see Coutinho and Benteke linking up, they could get deadly.

I really liked Moreno in the little we saw of him, he was making some dangerous pushes.

I have to agree with our performance, it was not very convincing and we play Arsenal next. Something quite annoying is that the defense played very well it was the midfield and moving forward that didn't seem to click.

It was the same against Stoke. I think we need to start with Can in midfield along side Henderson and Milner ( or choose one of the two to start......)

Bournemouth played really good, was very impressed with their performance.

If I was to rate it I would say most of the game we were about 6.5/10 with flashes of 8/10 while Bournemouth were consistant 8/10
Yeah now that you mention it the defense was pretty solid, we had quite a few stops in the box.

It was too reminiscent of last year. Midfield and attack were not linking up and playing as fluidly as would be expected. With a good few new players I am sure it will take time to gel. Let's just hope we show up against Arsenal, they haven't been too convincing themselves.

I know when you eat fruit you get fiber that slows the absorption down of the sugar, but does this apply to applesauce as well? The label only shows 1g of fiber, so my guess is no.

A small apple with the skin has 3.6 grams of fiber, and a medium-sized apple with the skin contains 4.4 grams. Eat a large apple with the skin and you'll get 5.4 grams of fiber.

Source

So maybe actually. It's not that much more in a whole apple. I think the apples are probably just so diluted in the applesauce that you would have to eat a whole bunch. There's 2g of fiber in this organic applesauce that I found online per 1/2 cup (3.2oz = 0.4cups) which is close to double I suppose, so maybe buying one with less additives would have more benefits.
